subject: NovaQuest: scaling, model-fit & SLO qualification
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: NovaQuest discovery — scaling, model-fit & SLOs (recap + next steps)

Hi Luis / Sarah — thanks again for the call today. Fast recap and the concrete next steps we discussed so we’re aligned:

Pain points / goals we heard
- Primary workload: clinical-document summarization + semantic search across patient notes (real-time assist for clinicians).
- Target 95th pctl latency: <= 200ms for single-turn summarization requests at peak (90–120 concurrent clinicians).
- Sustained throughput target: ~180–220 requests/sec during peak windows; spiky bursts up to ~400 req/s.
- Model quality: trustworthy summaries with hallucination controls and redaction of PHI. HIPAA compliance required.

Technical constraints called out
- Average prompt size: 1.2k tokens (long notes), typical response length 150–300 tokens.
- Payloads include structured patient metadata (small JSON) + free text.
- On-prem audit/logging and customer-managed keys preferred.

Redwood recommendation (high level)
- Private deployment in your AWS VPC using Redwood Private (dedicated capacity). Helps meet HIPAA and audit requirements while giving predictable throughput.
- Two-model strategy: smaller distilled model for summaries (low latency) + larger model for fallback/edge cases. Route by confidence & latency SLOs.
- Enable KV prefix caching for repeated context chunks (we’ll quantify savings after we see traces).

Attachments I’ll share: topology sketch + KV-cache microbenchmark (attached).

Immediate next steps
1) Technical deep-dive with our infra/ops (Marissa + Sean) to map SLOs to topology — can we do Tue/Wed next week? (proposed slots below)
2) You to share 48–72 hours of anonymized traffic samples (redact PHI) and a couple of example long notes for token distribution analysis.
3) Procurement: we’ll get a draft SOW/estimate once we size the committed capacity (procurement contact copied on next thread).

Proposed deep-dive times (PDT):
- Tue 19 May 10:00–11:00
- Wed 20 May 14:00–15:00

Thanks — I’ll book once you confirm availability.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0192

Kimberly — thanks for the clear summary. A few clarifications from our infra side before the deep-dive so Marissa can size things appropriately:

1) Concurrency / request shape: the 180–220 req/s is what our app emits after batching at the API level; per-user flows are mostly sequential but the UI does background prefetching. The 400 burst is observed during shift handovers.
2) Sequence lengths: 1.2k tokens average is correct, but ~10% of notes push 3–4k tokens. Those are the tricky edge-cases.
3) Data residency: all PHI must stay in our VPC; we can run Private with customer-managed keys.

Questions:
- Can Redwood guarantee p95 <= 200ms for the 1.2k token average on a distilled 7B model, or would that require quantized 8-bit on A100/HPU?
- For the long 3–4k notes, do you recommend server-side summarization pipeline (pre-chunk + merge) or a single long-context model variant?

We’re available Tue 19 May 10:00–11:00 PDT — that slot works for Marissa or Sean. I’ll send anonymized traces by EOD Monday.

Thanks,
Luis Martinez
CTO (Acting) — NovaQuest Health
luis.m@novaquest.com

Subject: NovaQuest — suggested topology and SLO mapping (pre-deep-dive notes)

Hi Luis / Kimberly — I pulled together a short tech-first sketch ahead of Tuesday’s deep-dive. High-level recommendations below; we’ll walk through details in the call.

1) Topology (recommended)- Private Redwood control plane + dedicated GPU fleet in your AWS account (VPC peering / transit gateway).
- Two-tier serving:
  * Tier A (low-latency): distilled 7B model quantized to 8-bit on A100s for p95 <= 200ms on ~1.2k token requests. Continuous batching (target batch 8–16, dynamic) and low token-slicing.
  * Tier B (high-fidelity): full 34B (or hosted LLM of your choice) for fallback when confidence below threshold — routed asynchronously or with graceful degrade.

2) Long-document handling- For 3–4k token notes: recommend pre-chunk+merge on ingest (server-side pipeline) + KV cache for repeating sections (e.g., SOAP headers). This keeps per-request latency bounded and allows you to hit SLOs without an expensive long-context model for every request.

3) SLO mapping (quick table)
- p50: 40–60ms (inference-only, distilled model)
- p95: <= 200ms (inference-only, with dynamic batching tuned to request patterns)
- availability: 99.9% monthly (with Dedicated commit + autoscale buffer)

4) Resource sizing notes (back-of-envelope)
- Sustained 200 req/s at ~1.2k tokens and batch=12 => ~16 A100 GPUs (dedicated pool) with autoscale to handle 400 burst with short warm-up capacity or fallback routing. We’ll refine with your traces.

5) Observability & safety- Suggest shipping a small eval set + hallucination checks so we can tune model thresholds. Include audit logs and request-level token accounting for billing/SOC2 evidence.

Attachments: kv_cache_benchmark.csv (sample cache hit savings), topology_sketch_v1.pdf

Ask before Tuesday’s deep-dive
- Please share 48–72h anonymized traffic and a handful of long-note examples (no PHI).
- Confirm whether procurement needs an estimated committed GPU count for SOW drafting.

I’ll be on the Tue 19 May 10:00–11:00 PDT slot.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
